summary.title: Schneier on Security
summary.one_liner: Bruce Schneier's security blog collects short commentary and links on current security news, research papers, and incidents such as weak TLS keys, PHP vulnerabilities, and bias in Chinese AI coding models.
keywords: weis economics of information security archive
takeaways: Weak private keys in eMudhra TLS certificates (as small as 3 to 8 bits) show how one certificate authority can undermine TLS, and active man-in-the-middle position is needed to exploit them.
Two critical PHP vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote code execution; PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 contain fixes and users are urged to update.
Research found Chinese-origin Qwen3-Coder produces less secure code depending on stated end user, and removing CCP alignment closed those gaps.
Several linked research papers cover hidden backdoor capabilities in AI models and VLM-based CAPTCHA solvers that improve with use.
summary.summary: This is the front page of Bruce Schneier's security blog, showing a rolling list of short posts with excerpts and links to news and research. Each entry summarizes an item and quotes sources, such as reports on weak eMudhra TLS keys, critical PHP vulnerabilities, Cellebrite's Advanced Unlocks product leaked to Justin.sh, and academic papers on hidden AI capabilities and adaptive CAPTCHA solvers. The page also includes a reader squid-post thread and a note on the WEIS workshop paper archive. It is a news and commentary feed rather than a structured tutorial.
